$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for apps/core-api's WIN-260 (M2.5) shutdown work: the
admission gate in src/runtime/in-flight.ts, the deferred-drain sequence in
src/runtime/shutdown-drain.ts, and their wiring in src/runtime/lifecycle.ts.
One entry per invariant, each carrying the file it lives in, the EXACT text
that implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED
cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
A guard nothing can turn red is a guard that is not there — and this sweep
found two of those in code this dimension had just written. C03 and C14 are
NOTHING HERE NEEDS A DATABASE OR A CONTAINER. Every case runs against a real
in-process HTTP server or against the sequence's own injected clock, which is
why the whole ledger is swept in about four seconds.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. An earlier tranche reported 22 kills and every
one was VACUOUS: a package's dist/ had been cleaned, so every suite failed to
LOAD and would have 'died' against no mutation at all. The driver runs each
suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep unless it is green, and classifies a
module-load failure with no named failing case as VACUOUS.
For one entry: replace its `from` with its `to` in the named file, run
`pnpm --filter @platos/core-api exec vitest run <suites>`, and confirm a NAMED
case goes red. Then revert and confirm green.
so its case count is not pinned there. It is pinned by
docs/v1-ledger-rules.json's apps-core-api.test.suites FILE count and by this
ledger, which names cases rather than counting them.

mutations.name: C14 the settle idempotence flag — DECLARED UNFALSIFIABLE, with the measured reason
unfalsifiable: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: the mutation was applied and the whole suite stayed
green, including the case named `settles idempotently, because Express fires
WHY. The register holds a `Map` keyed by registration id, not a counter.
`running.delete(id)` on an id already deleted is a no-op, so a double
settle cannot take the count below zero with or without the flag. The
comment that used to stand beside it said 'without this guard the counter
would go negative', which described an implementation this file does not
have; the prose is corrected in the source rather than left to be believed.
THE FLAG IS KEPT as an early return — it is free and it documents intent —
and it is recorded here as a guard that CANNOT be turned red rather than
counted as a kill that was not obtained. The property it appears to protect
IS covered, by the Map itself and by the named case above, which fails if
`running.delete(id)` is replaced by a numeric decrement.
